head: pr17412-r6
report:
There's a FIFO deferral path. Reading it — this is exactly a check-then-use shape.

I found one defect in the class you asked about. I could not run it on the commit under review: the native addon in the snapshot is a symlink to `/mnt/nvme/tmp-omp-batch/reviewer-gap-rederive/donor/natives/pi_natives.linux-x64-modern.node`. That build was not made from f8cddb4, because none of this patch's new strings appear in it (for example "already waiting on a peer"). Cargo is unavailable, so I could not build it either. The measurement below therefore comes from the donor addon. The code involved is the same at head, since the patch moves it without changing it, but at head the result is an inference.

## 1. `$(<fifo)` inside a background external command reads `/dev/null`, not the FIFO

**Where**
- **T1**, `crates/vendor/brush-core/src/commands.rs:1178`: `let mut params = params.clone();` copies the caller's parameters, including `defer_fifo_redirects`. That flag is set at `interp.rs:724` for a background external command.
- **Then**, `commands.rs:1192`: `interp::setup_redirect(&mut subshell, &mut params, redir)` reaches `interp.rs:2443-2456`. Because the flag is set and the target is a native FIFO (`child_open`/`is_native_fifo`), it records a `DeferredRedirect` for a child that never exists and returns `Ok(())` without touching fd 0.
- **T2**, `commands.rs:1193`: `read_to_end_detached(params.stdin(&subshell))` reads fd 0 again. The code assumes the redirect just installed it, but fd 0 is still the `/dev/null` that `spawn_async_ao_list_as_job` set (`interp.rs:709-711`).

**What changes in the window:** `setup_redirect` decides to defer the open instead of making it. Nothing deferred is ever materialized on this path, so the substitution yields `""`. Nobody ever opens the FIFO for reading, so a writer on it blocks until the run's timeout.

**Trigger**
```sh
rm -f f; mkfifo f; (sleep 0.3; echo data > f) & /bin/echo "bg=[$(<f)]" & wait
```
bash prints `bg=[data]`.

**Measured** with `fifo.test.ts` in the scratch dir, run on the donor addon via `executeShell`, 5 s timeout:
```
$ bun test --timeout 30000 .../fifo.test.ts
"rm -f f; mkfifo f; (sleep 0.3; echo data > f) & /bin/echo \"fg=[$(<f)]\"; wait" => "fg=[data]\n" {"timedOut":false,"exitCode":0,...}
"rm -f f; mkfifo f; (sleep 0.3; echo data > f) & /bin/echo \"bg=[$(<f)]\" & wait" => "bg=[]\nerror: failed to redirect to .../f: Operation canceled (os error 125)\nerror: interrupted\n" {"cancelled":false,"timedOut":true}
"printf data > r; /bin/echo \"bgfile=[$(<r)]\" & wait" => "bgfile=[data]\n" {"timedOut":false,"exitCode":0,...}

$ timeout 5 bash -c '<same bg command>'
bg=[data]
exit=0
```
The foreground and regular-file controls are correct. Only the background-plus-FIFO case is wrong: it prints the empty value, the writer hangs in `open`, and the run times out.

**Why it matters for this patch:** the bug predates the patch. But the patch rewrote this exact `$(<file)` shortcut, moving it out of `run_substitution_command` into `invoke_command_in_subshell_and_get_output`. The CHANGELOG entry also claims `$(<file)` is now fixed "whether the file ... is a FIFO nobody writes to". On this path it returns wrong data and leaves the other end of the FIFO stuck.

**Fix:** the substitution has to use the redirect it set up, not whatever fd 0 is afterwards. Clear `params.defer_fifo_redirects` on the substitution's own `params` before `setup_redirect`, so it opens the FIFO itself. Alternatively, call `materialize_deferred_redirects` before `params.stdin(...)`.

## 2. The cap on waiting reads is one counter for the whole process (not measured)

**Where:** `crates/vendor/brush-core/src/openfiles.rs`, `DETACHED_SIDES` and `DETACHED_SIDE_LIMIT = 64`.

**Mechanism:** the limit is counted per process, but the threads it counts belong to individual runs. A permit is released only when its thread returns, and a thread parked on a FIFO nobody writes to, or on a socket that never answers, never returns.

**Trigger:** in one shell session, run 64 commands that each time out inside `$(</dev/fd/N)` on a pipe nobody writes to. After that, every other session in the same agent process gets `ResourceBusy` on any `$(<pipe-or-terminal)` until those peers act.

This needs the head build to measure, so it stays a hypothesis.

## Also noted
`openfiles::copy_async` no longer has a production caller. After this patch only `crates/pi-shell/tests/substitution_copy.rs` uses it, so it is a public function kept alive only by its tests.

## Re-lookups I checked and found sound
- **`try_resolve_parameter_to_variable`** now returns only the name, and its callers look the variable up again (`expansion.rs:1452-1467`). There is no `await` between the two lookups, so the result matches the old cloned copy.
- **`update_or_add` / `assign_array`** hold `&mut` borrows of the variable across their checkpoint awaits, so no other shell code can change it in between. `value_converter()` takes its copy of the attributes under that same borrow.
- **`CopySide::classify`** checks the descriptor's type once with `fstat`. The type of an open descriptor cannot change afterwards.
